title: Feature ledger — v1.0
description: plan.md §16.4, chainlink #34. A GENERATED, READ-ONLY projection, same tier as the Stage 4.5 contact sheet (§16.3): derived entirely from already-normative or already-generated artifacts, itself normative of nothing. Machine-emitted at ci/results/feature_ledger.json; no `review` block, for the same reason a C_static report or an achieved assurance record carries none -- a human freely authoring what was 'observed' would be indistinguishable from fabricating a result. Never consulted by satisfies(), assurance computation, or closure computation (§16.6's boundary): it reports on those mechanisms, it does not participate in them. The two-column discipline is the whole reason this file exists: `implementation_observed` (a weak liveness fact -- the body executed on its fixture and produced a stable, non-degenerate value) and `assurance_status` (the contract is established, from the owning obligation's validated assurance record) are NEVER the same bit and are NEVER inferred from each other -- the identical discipline this plan already applies to `closure_kind` vs. coverage.

generated_from.description: sha256 over a canonical (sorted-key, compact-separator JSON, canonical-json-v1 style) serialization of every input artifact actually consulted while generating this ledger, sorted by path -- so the SAME workspace state always produces the SAME hashes, and a changed input is visible here before it is visible in `features`.

concept_specs_hash.description: Over every concept spec (vendor/concept-to-code layer) that owns at least one declared (witness_required: true) feature.

witness_specs_hash.description: Over every genuinely valid witness spec discovered workspace-wide (validate_witness.py's own G1a/G1b/G2 bar), regardless of whether it backs a declared feature.

assurance_results_hash.description: Over every genuinely schema-valid work-package assurance report reachable from a schema-valid manifest's own report.emit path, workspace-wide.

features.description: One entry per DECLARED feature (a concept-to-code query with witness_required: true) -- coverage here is relative to the declared set only, the identical boundary chainlink #29's G18 already draws: an undeclared query is invisible to this ledger, exactly as R2 stays invisible to an undeclared interaction.

feature.description: <Concept>.<query> -- the same identity a witness spec's own concept/query pair names.

witness_required.description: Always true: only witness_required: true queries are declared features and appear here at all. Present explicitly rather than left implicit, matching plan.md §16.4's own worked example.

witness_present.description: chainlink #29's G18 disposition for this feature: a genuinely valid witness spec exists, its declared rendering exists on disk, and it is not ambiguous.

implementation_observed.description: The WEAK liveness fact only: the body executed on its fixture and produced a stable, non-degenerate value. True only when witness_present is true AND the witness's canonical result genuinely matches this spec's own identity (never trusted on witness_id alone) AND chainlink #30's G19 (determinism) and #31's G20 (degeneracy) both dispose clean for it. Never implies, and must never be read as, assurance -- see assurance_status.

determinism.description: chainlink #30's G19 disposition for this feature's witness. not-checked when there is no witness to check, or no witness_backend is configured in the project descriptor (nothing was actually re-evaluated, which is a different fact from a real mismatch).

degeneracy.description: chainlink #31's G20 disposition for this feature's witness. not-checked when there is no witness to check.

assurance_status.description: The CONTRACT, from the owning obligation's validated assurance record -- never inferred from witness_present, implementation_observed, determinism, or degeneracy. A green witness proves the body runs on one fixture; it proves nothing about the contract. Currently always 'unsupported': see generate_feature_ledger.py's own module docstring for why no mechanical link between a witnessed query and an obligation exists yet in this codebase.

owning_cluster.description: The concept spec's own top-level `cluster` field (vendor/concept-to-code's schema, already domain-agnostic and required) -- read directly, not re-derived.

closure_kind.description: The owning cluster's genuinely valid closure profile's own declared closure_kind (docs/closure-profile-schema.json), or 'n/a' when no genuinely valid closure profile exists for this cluster. Kept strictly separate from witness/coverage state, the same discipline plan.md §16.4 already names.
